candidates.name: deterministic-checks-not-llm
candidates.objection: The core principle is plausibly already covered by jpcaparas/skills@heuristic-to-deterministic (40 installs) in the ecosystemSearch output — the generic 'replace model heuristics with deterministic checks' idea is not bespoke. What IS bespoke and worth keeping is the repo-specific enforcement layer: RISK_RE word-anchored routing, Set-lookup evidence verification, and the fail-closed rule that deterministic findings are handed to LLM reviewers as non-overrulable confirmed defects. Extend the existing skill with those invariants rather than building a parallel statement of the general principle.
candidates.justification: The ecosystem search surfaced jpcaparas/skills@heuristic-to-deterministic (40 installs), which by name and the skeptic's assessment already covers the generic principle of replacing model-based heuristics with deterministic checks — building a parallel restatement of that principle would create skill sprawl. However, the candidate's real value is not the general principle but this repo's enforcement layer: RISK_RE word-anchored gate routing with no LLM in the loop, Set-lookup verification of cited evidence paths, sha256 whole-directory fingerprinting, deterministic report rendering (avoiding model-rendered tables that drop rows), and the fail-closed invariant that deterministic findings are passed to LLM reviewers as confirmed, non-overrulable defects. None of that repo-specific contract is plausibly present in the public skill. EXTEND is therefore correct: adopt heuristic-to-deterministic as the base statement of the principle and author a thin overlay documenting the fail-closed enforcement invariants and the specific modules (src/evidence.js, src/grounding.js, src/fingerprint.js, src/gates.js, src/report.js) that implement them. Caveat worth recording: the search output provides only names and install counts, so the overlay author should verify the base skill's actual content covers the general principle before finalizing; if it does not, escalate to BUILD.

skills.name: safe-subprocess-invocation
skills.verification: **Gate B** @ 2026-07-20: used cold vs "Add a local Codex CLI fallback to src/llm.js that invokes `codex exec` as a child process using execFile with an argv array (no shell strings), guards command detection against the Windows .cmd shim charset issue, ignores stderr noise, applies a timeout, and closes stdin to prevent hangs." (real commit b17b42b) → SHIP; fixes applied (1 round(s)): Step 6 mandates using execCliIgnoringStderr from src/llm.js but never documents its signature or contract: a cold agent cannot tell whether it accepts a timeout option, whether it closes the child's stdin internally, or what it returns (stdout string? object?). The test task requires 'applies a timeout' and 'closes stdin' — following the skill literally, the agent cannot verify either requirement is satisfied when routing through this helper, and may either omit the timeout entirely or double-handle stdin.; Step 5 (always call child.stdin.end()) and Step 6 (use execCliIgnoringStderr, whose stdio is ['pipe','pipe','ignore'] so stdin is a pipe) are in unresolved tension: the skill never states whether the helper ends stdin for you. A missing stdin.end() 'presents as a timeout, not an error' per the skill's own warning, so this ambiguity reproduces exactly the failure class the skill exists to prevent.; The only timeout constants the skill names (WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS=60000, SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS=15000) belong to src/dedupe.js and are semantically about npx skills searches. For the codex-exec call in src/llm.js the agent must invent a timeout value and constant name with no guidance — LLM CLI invocations plausibly need a much larger budget than 15s, and the Conventions section ('every subprocess call has an explicit timeout') gives no number for this call class.
